newsitem.title: USA: Missouri $575 mln sales tax increase edges forward.
newsitem.headline: Missouri $575 mln sales tax increase edges forward.

text.p: A Missouri transportation panel has moved closer to endorsing a $575 million sales tax increase to rescue an embattled highway and bridge-building program, a spokesman said Wednesday.
During a meeting Tuesday, the Missouri Total Transportation Commission agreed on a comprehensive transportation plan for the state, said Jim Gardner, a spokesman for the commissiom.
A subcommittee of the panel recommended increasing the state sales tax by 1 percent, which would initially raise $575 million a year.
Gardner said it was likely that the full 35-member commission would eventually approve the sales tax increase and present its recommendation to Missouri Gov. Mel Carnahan by July 2.
Carnahan could then accept or reject the tax increase or recommend something different to the legislature. Voters would have the final say on any proposal.

The overall plan would raise about $13 billion over 16 years. Most of the money -- $10.7 billion -- would go to highways; the rest would be split between improving public transit, aviation and passenger rail service.
Missouri legislators approved a transportation improvement plan in 1992 financed by gradually increasing the state gasoline tax.
But it was revealed last year that the program was seriously underfunded, and that an additional $14 billion was needed to finish projects promised earlier.
Talk of raising the state sales tax, which is currently 4.225 percent, comes just weeks after Missouri lawmakers and Carnahan scrapped the state's 3 percent general sales tax on food.
Commission members conceded that the move to increase the general sales tax likely will face opposition from the state's retailers and could also roil voters.
"This is not going to be easy," S. Lee Kling, chairman of the commission, told the Kansas City Star newspaper. "It's a lot of money, but what else are you going to do?"
